name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
thesis: NVIDIA is still growing faster than its suppliers can add capacity: Q2 FY27 revenue was $96.2B (+106% y/y) with a $108B Q3 guide, and the Big 4 hyperscalers plan roughly $725B+ of 2026 capex with 2027 modeled above $1T. The money that flows through NVIDIA is now being captured by whoever owns the scarcest input, which in late 2026 is HBM and DRAM, CoWoS and substrates (ABF film, T-glass), lasers and fiber, and above all electric power (gas turbines, transformers, switchgear). The best risk/reward picks and shovels are chokepoint suppliers with pricing power and multiyear contracts (SK hynix, Micron, TSMC, ASML, Advantest, Amphenol, Credo, Lumentum, Corning, GE Vernova, Vertiv) rather than thin-margin assemblers. The Rubin transition (100% liquid cooled, HBM4, M9 boards, 1.6T optics) and Kyber (600 kW racks on 800V DC) raise content per rack for cooling, power, optics and boards, but Rubin's mainstream ramp may slip into 2027 on HBM. The main threats are a capex pause, custom ASICs (TPU, Trainium) taking share, and Taiwan concentration.

facts: Q2 FY2027 (quarter ended Jul 26, 2026, reported Aug 26, 2026): revenue $96.2B, up 106% y/y and 18% q/q; Data Center revenue $89.0B, up 117% y/y.
Q2 FY2027 GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin 75.0%; Q3 FY2027 guide about $108B +/-2% revenue with gross margin about 74%.
Inventory rose to $31.6B in Q2 FY2027 ahead of the Vera Rubin launch; management reported initial Vera Rubin production shipments.
Networking revenue was $14.8B in Q1 FY2027 (up 199% y/y) and rose 18% q/q to a record in Q2 FY2027; Spectrum-X Ethernet revenue grew 2.6x y/y.
NVIDIA booked an estimated 800-850k TSMC CoWoS wafers for 2026, roughly 60% of capacity (industry reports, 2026).
NVIDIA invested $2B each in Lumentum and Coherent (March 2026) tied to multi-billion-dollar laser and optics purchase commitments.

China: H20 license requirement led to a $4.5B charge in Q1 FY2026; BIS moved to case-by-case review for H200 on Jan 13, 2026, and NVIDIA said at GTC 2026 it had licenses and POs for multiple Chinese customers.

pipeline.timing: Full volume production through 2026; Blackwell family projected at about 71% of NVIDIA high-end GPU shipments in 2026 (TrendForce)
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Volume workhorse for 2026: HBM3E 12-Hi (SK hynix, Micron, Samsung), TSMC 4NP and CoWoS-L, ConnectX-8 and 800G/1.6T optics, Amphenol NVLink copper spine, ~130 kW racks with liquid cooling. Keeps current suppliers full while Rubin ramps.

pipeline.product: Vera Rubin NVL144 / VR200 NVL72 (Rubin GPU, Vera CPU, CX9, BlueField-4)
pipeline.timing: Initial production shipments in Aug 2026 quarter per NVIDIA; NVIDIA expects Rubin to be a growing share from Q3 FY27. TrendForce (Sep 2026) says the mainstream ramp slips to 2027 on HBM4 snags; UBS (May 2026) flagged rack cooling issues.
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: HBM4 (288GB per GPU; SK hynix lead, Samsung second, Micron smaller), TSMC N3 and larger CoWoS-L, 100% liquid cooled fanless trays (more cold plates, CDUs, quick disconnects), M9 laminate with quartz cloth and HVLP copper foil, 1.6T optics and NVLink 6. Higher dollar content per rack for memory, boards, cooling and optics.

pipeline.product: Spectrum-X / Quantum-X Photonics co-packaged optics switches
pipeline.timing: Spectrum-X Photonics shipping from 2H 2026; scale-up CPO volume 2H 2027 to 2028 (Lumentum)
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Moves the optical engine onto the switch package: winners are external laser makers (Lumentum, Coherent), fiber array and connector makers (Corning, Browave, SENKO, TFC), TSMC COUPE packaging and Besi hybrid bonding. Long term threat to pluggable transceiver makers (Innolight, Eoptolink, Fabrinet volume).

600 kW racks on 800V DC distribution with vertical blade trays: big step up for power electronics (Delta, MPS, Infineon, Navitas, Vertiv, Eaton), solid-state transformers and liquid cooling. HBM4E 12-Hi planned but NVIDIA is evaluating lower HBM configurations because of DRAM shortage (TrendForce Aug 2026). Very high layer count (reported 78-layer) midplane PCB is a supply risk.

pipeline.product: Feynman (Rosa CPU, LP40 LPU, BlueField-5, NVLink 8 CPO, Spectrum-7 CPO, CX10)
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Die stacking (hybrid bonding: Besi, Applied Materials), custom HBM base dies, co-packaged optics for scale-up NVLink (shifts some copper content to optics and lasers), Kyber NVL1152 racks. Likely TSMC A16-class process (unverified).

layers.name: Raw and specialty materials
layers.why: Every GPU starts as a polished silicon wafer and ends on a substrate built from Japanese films and glass cloth; a few niche materials makers sit upstream of everything else and have little competition.
layers.bottleneck_reason: ABF film (Ajinomoto) and low-CTE T-glass cloth (Nittobo, about 90% share) are near monopolies running at full capacity; T-glass has a 10%+ supply gap in 2026 with new capacity not before mid-2027, and Ajinomoto is reported to be raising ABF film prices about 30%. China's gallium/germanium export ban to the US is only suspended until Nov 27, 2026.

companies.name: Shin-Etsu Chemical
companies.role: Largest maker of 300mm silicon wafers; also photoresist and other wafer materials
companies.note: Foreign; OTC ADR SHECY. Wafer duopoly with SUMCO.

companies.name: SUMCO
companies.role: Number two 300mm silicon wafer maker
companies.note: Foreign; OTC ADR SUMCY.

companies.name: Ajinomoto
companies.role: Makes ABF (Ajinomoto Build-up Film), the insulating film inside every advanced chip substrate
companies.note: Foreign; OTC ADR AJINY. Near monopoly on ABF; lines reported at full capacity, price hike of 30%+ reported in 2026. Food is most of revenue.

companies.name: Nitto Boseki (Nittobo)
companies.role: Makes T-glass (low-CTE glass cloth) for substrates and NER glass for high-speed PCBs
companies.note: Foreign. About 90% of T-glass; NVIDIA, Microsoft, Google, Amazon booked most premium capacity for 2026.

companies.name: Tokyo Ohka Kogyo (TOK)
companies.role: Leading photoresist supplier for EUV and advanced nodes
companies.note: Foreign. Japanese firms dominate photoresist; JSR, another leader, was taken private.

companies.name: Linde
companies.role: Industrial and specialty gases (nitrogen, hydrogen, rare gases) for fabs, on-site plants at TSMC and others

companies.name: Entegris
companies.role: Filters, purification, CMP slurries and specialty chemicals used at every advanced node

companies.name: Freeport-McMoRan
companies.role: Copper miner; copper goes into busbars, power cables, cooling plates and grid equipment
companies.note: Indirect, commodity driven.

companies.name: MP Materials
companies.role: US rare earth mining and magnets; hedge against China rare earth controls (magnets used in motors, fans, pumps, turbines)
companies.note: Indirect.

layers.name: Semiconductor equipment (lithography, deposition/etch, inspection, test, bonding)
layers.why: TSMC, SK hynix and the packaging houses can only add capacity as fast as these tools ship; AI pushes more EUV layers, more HBM stacking steps and much longer test times.
layers.bottleneck_reason: ASML is the only EUV supplier and says 2027 EUV capacity is nearly fully booked (Q2 2026). Test is a hidden bottleneck: an AI accelerator can need 20+ minutes on a tester versus under a minute for a phone chip, and Advantest plus Teradyne hold over 90% of SoC test.

companies.name: ASML Holding
companies.role: Sole supplier of EUV lithography (including High-NA)
companies.note: ADR. Raised 2026 revenue guide to EUR 43-45B in Q2 2026; adding ~30% EUV capacity for 2027.

companies.name: Applied Materials
companies.role: Deposition, etch, CMP; co-developed hybrid bonding line with BESI (first SK hynix volume order Mar 2026)

companies.name: Lam Research
companies.role: Etch and deposition, critical for HBM through-silicon vias and 3D structures

companies.name: Tokyo Electron
companies.role: Coater/developers paired with every EUV tool, plus etch and deposition
companies.note: Foreign; OTC ADR TOELY. Near monopoly on EUV coater/developer tracks.

companies.name: KLA
companies.role: Process control and inspection; dominant share in wafer and reticle inspection

companies.name: Advantest
companies.role: SoC and memory testers; SoC test share rose from about 56% to 66%; HBM is about half its memory test business
companies.note: Foreign; OTC ADR ATEYY. Main tester for NVIDIA GPUs.

companies.name: Teradyne
companies.role: SoC and memory test; Q1 2026 revenue up 87% y/y with about 70% from AI
companies.note: Duopoly with Advantest.

companies.name: BE Semiconductor (Besi)
companies.role: Hybrid bonding and advanced die attach for HBM4E/HBM5, logic stacking and co-packaged optics
companies.note: Foreign; OTC BESIY. Q1 2026 orders EUR 269.7M, more than double y/y.

companies.name: Disco
companies.role: Dicing, grinding and thinning tools needed for thin HBM dies and CoWoS
companies.note: Foreign; OTC DSCSY. Dominant share.

companies.name: Hanmi Semiconductor
companies.role: Thermo-compression bonders used to stack HBM at SK hynix
companies.note: Foreign.

layers.name: Foundry and advanced packaging (CoWoS and successors)
layers.why: Every NVIDIA data center GPU is built at TSMC and joined to its HBM on TSMC's CoWoS interposer; CoWoS capacity has set the ceiling on GPU output since 2023.
layers.bottleneck_reason: TSMC is a single point of failure for leading-edge logic and CoWoS. NVIDIA has booked about 800-850k CoWoS wafers for 2026, roughly 60% of capacity; year-end 2026 capacity estimates range from 95k to 140k wafers per month. TSMC is now outsourcing a front-end CoWoS step to OSATs (TrendForce, Aug 2026).

companies.name: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC)
companies.role: Makes NVIDIA GPUs (4N, N3 for Rubin) and does CoWoS-L packaging
companies.note: ADR. Aug 2026 revenue NT$514.8B, up 53.3% y/y, first month over NT$500B.

companies.name: ASE Technology (incl. SPIL)
companies.role: Largest OSAT; takes overflow CoWoS-type steps and final test for AI chips
companies.note: ADR.

companies.name: Amkor Technology
companies.role: OSAT building advanced packaging in Arizona near TSMC's US fabs

companies.name: Intel
companies.role: Foundry and EMIB/Foveros packaging alternative; High-NA EUV in volume production at Intel per ASML
companies.note: Second source option, not yet a major NVIDIA supplier for data center GPUs.

layers.name: Memory (HBM)
layers.why: Each Rubin GPU carries 288GB of HBM4; HBM is now the scarcest and most expensive component after the GPU die itself, and it is the main reason Rubin's mainstream ramp is slipping.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Only three suppliers; TrendForce (Sep 2026) says Rubin's ramp slips to 2027 on HBM snags and DRAM stays tight through 2027. Conventional DRAM contract prices rose about 90-95% in Q1 2026 and 58-63% in Q2 2026 (TrendForce).

companies.name: SK hynix
companies.role: Lead HBM3E and HBM4 supplier to NVIDIA; about 54% of 2026 HBM4 (Counterpoint)
companies.note: Foreign. Q2 2026 operating profit KRW 60.5T, record; began HBM4 mass shipments in Q2 2026.

companies.name: Samsung Electronics
companies.role: Second HBM4 supplier for Rubin (about 28% share est.); also a foundry
companies.note: Foreign. Started HBM4 shipments Feb 2026. Q3 2026 preliminary operating profit about KRW 107.4T, a record, up 782.5% y/y (Oct 8, 2026).

companies.name: Micron Technology
companies.role: Third HBM supplier (about 18% HBM4 share est.); only US-listed memory maker
companies.note: FQ4 2026 (ended Sep 3) revenue $54.23B; FY2026 $133.19B; FQ1 2027 guide ~$61.5B.

layers.name: Substrates, PCBs and laminates
layers.why: The GPU package sits on an ABF substrate and the rack runs on very high-layer-count boards; Rubin moves to M9-grade laminates with quartz glass cloth and HVLP copper foil, which raises content value per rack.
layers.bottleneck_reason: ABF substrate supply gap seen lasting through 2027; copper clad laminate prices rose 20% to 40%+ in 1H 2026 with lead times up to 140 days; quartz cloth for M9 is in extreme shortage. Kyber's 78-layer midplane PCB is reported as a design risk.

companies.name: Ibiden
companies.role: Leading ABF substrate maker for NVIDIA GPU packages
companies.note: Foreign; OTC IBIDF.

companies.name: Unimicron
companies.role: Largest Taiwan ABF substrate maker, high utilization
companies.note: Foreign.

companies.name: Elite Material (EMC)
companies.role: High-end copper clad laminate (M8/M9) for AI server boards
companies.note: Foreign. Role widely reported; share unverified.

companies.name: Victory Giant Technology
companies.role: High-layer PCBs and HDI for NVIDIA AI servers

companies.name: Mitsui Mining and Smelting
companies.role: HVLP ultra-low-profile copper foil for high-speed boards
companies.note: Foreign. HVLP capacity reported short; share unverified.

companies.name: TTM Technologies
companies.role: US PCB maker for data center and networking boards

layers.name: Networking: switches, NICs, SerDes, optics, CPO, AECs, fiber
layers.why: AI clusters are only as fast as the links between GPUs; networking is NVIDIA's fastest growing line (Q1 FY27 networking revenue $14.8B, Spectrum-X up 2.6x y/y in Q2 FY27) and pulls optics, copper cables and fiber with it.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Indium phosphide lasers (Lumentum, Coherent) and fiber are capacity limited; NVIDIA paid $2B each into Lumentum and Coherent (Mar 2026) to secure laser supply, and three hyperscalers signed multiyear fiber deals with Corning in 2026.

companies.name: Broadcom
companies.role: Tomahawk Ethernet switch silicon, PCIe switches, SerDes, CPO; also the main custom ASIC (TPU) rival
companies.note: Supplier to the ecosystem and the biggest competitive threat via custom chips.

companies.name: Arista Networks
companies.role: Ethernet switches for AI back-end and front-end networks

companies.name: Credo Technology
companies.role: Active electrical cables (AECs) and SerDes; about 88% AEC share (JPMorgan est.)
companies.note: FQ3 2026 revenue $407M, up 202% y/y; top 3 customers 88% of revenue.

companies.name: Astera Labs
companies.role: PCIe/CXL retimers, Scorpio fabric switches, NVLink Fusion connectivity
companies.note: Q1 2026 revenue $308.4M, up 93% y/y; NVLink Fusion revenue expected from 2027.

companies.name: Marvell Technology
companies.role: Optical DSPs for transceivers, custom XPUs, CPO
companies.note: Also custom ASIC competitor. Raised fiscal 2028 revenue target to about $20 billion (from $18 billion) and set a fiscal 2031 goal of $70 to $90 billion at its Oct 6, 2026 investor day.

companies.name: Lumentum

companies.note: NVIDIA invested $2B (Mar 2026) with multi-billion purchase commitment.

companies.note: NVIDIA invested $2B (Mar 2026); scale-out CPO revenue from 2H 2026.

companies.note: Volume shipments of 1.6T began 2026.

companies.note: Foreign (China).

companies.name: Corning
companies.role: Optical fiber and connectivity; deals with Meta (up to $6B), NVIDIA (up to $3.2B) and Amazon in 2026; also fiber array units for CPO
companies.note: Optical Communications Q1 2026 sales $1.85B, up 36%.

companies.name: Celestica
companies.role: Builds hyperscaler Ethernet switches and AI racks

layers.name: Server assembly and ODMs
layers.why: ODMs turn trays into 1.5-2 ton liquid-cooled racks; they capture large revenue but thin margins, and their rack test capacity gates how fast new architectures ship.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Several qualified assemblers exist, but rack-level integration is hard: UBS reported Rubin rack cooling issues pushed rack mass production toward September 2026.

companies.role: Largest NVIDIA rack assembler and GPU board maker; reported up to ~60% of new Rubin server production
companies.note: Foreign; OTC ADR HNHPF.

companies.name: Quanta Computer
companies.role: Rack-scale ODM for hyperscalers (GB300, Rubin)
companies.note: Foreign.

companies.name: Wistron
companies.role: GPU baseboards and compute trays
companies.note: Foreign.

companies.name: Wiwynn

companies.note: Foreign.

companies.name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise

layers.name: Connectors and cables inside the rack
layers.why: The NVL72/NVL144 rack uses a copper NVLink spine with thousands of high-speed connections; copper stays inside the rack while optics take over between racks.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Amphenol dominates the NVLink copper backplane, but content can shift to optics (CPO) by the Feynman generation.

companies.name: Amphenol
companies.role: NVLink copper cable cartridges, high-speed connectors, power interconnect; CommScope fiber assets
companies.note: Q2 2026 sales $8.8B, up 55%; IT datacom up 89% and 43% of sales; book-to-bill 1.23.

companies.name: TE Connectivity
companies.role: High-speed and power connectors for AI servers

layers.name: Power delivery inside the rack
layers.why: Rack power is going from about 130 kW (GB300) to 600 kW (Rubin Ultra Kyber), forcing a shift to 800V DC, solid-state transformers, and GaN/SiC power chips.
layers.bottleneck_reason: The 800V DC ecosystem is new and needs qualified parts by the Kyber ramp in 2027; many chip vendors are competing, so supply is broad but designs are not yet locked.

companies.role: Power shelves, busbars and sidecar CDUs for NVIDIA racks; leader in sidecar CDUs
companies.note: Foreign.

companies.note: Small cap, speculative; revenue still small.

companies.name: onsemi

layers.name: Liquid cooling
layers.why: Vera Rubin is designed to be 100% liquid cooled and fanless; liquid cooling penetration among AI chips is seen rising from ~33% (2025) to ~53% (2026) and ~60% (2027) per TrendForce.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Many suppliers, but cold plates, quick disconnects and CDUs need qualification, and leak or cooling issues have delayed rack ramps.

companies.note: Q2 2026 sales $3.27B up 24%; backlog ~$15B; book-to-bill 2.9x; 2026 sales guide ~$14B.

layers.name: Data center construction and electrical contractors

layers.bottleneck_reason: Record backlogs everywhere (Quanta Services $53B, EMCOR RPO $17.1B, Comfort Systems $12.45B) and long switchgear and breaker lead times (HV breakers ~125 weeks).

second_order.why: Nittobo (about 90% of T-glass) and Ajinomoto (ABF film) are tiny parts of the bill of materials but cannot be substituted quickly; both are raising prices and capacity relief is not due until 2027-2028.
An AI accelerator with HBM can need 20+ minutes on a tester versus under a minute for a phone chip, so test capacity grows faster than unit volume; Advantest and Teradyne hold over 90% of SoC test.
With grid connections and turbines sold out for years, operators are building their own power; Oracle chose Bloom as sole power for a 2.45 GW campus.

second_order.idea: Fiber and lasers become the next shortage
second_order.why: Corning signed three multiyear hyperscaler fiber deals in 2026 (Meta up to $6B, NVIDIA up to $3.2B, Amazon) and NVIDIA prepaid $4B to secure lasers; co-packaged optics adds more fiber and laser content per switch.
Skilled electricians and switchgear install are scarce; record backlogs (Quanta $53B, EMCOR $17.1B, Comfort $12.45B) give multiyear visibility that is less exposed to GPU generation risk.

risks.risk: China export controls and retaliation (US chip rules; China gallium, germanium, rare earth curbs)
risks.signal: BIS license decisions on H200-class chips; whether China's suspension of its gallium/germanium export ban lapses on Nov 27, 2026; MOFCOM rare earth licensing.

risks.risk: Taiwan concentration (TSMC fabs and CoWoS, ODMs, substrates all in Taiwan)
risks.signal: Cross-strait military activity, shipping insurance costs, pace of TSMC Arizona advanced packaging.

risks.risk: Hyperscaler capex cut or AI ROI disappointment
risks.signal: Quarterly capex guides from MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META; neocloud financing spreads; Meta stock fell ~6% on its July 2026 capex raise, showing investor sensitivity.

risks.risk: Custom ASIC competition (Google TPU, AWS Trainium, Broadcom/Marvell XPUs)
risks.signal: Broadcom AI revenue (targets over $100B of AI chip revenue in 2027); Google TPU deals (Anthropic up to 1M TPUs, Meta); NVIDIA share of CoWoS bookings.

risks.risk: Power and grid constraints delay GPU deployments
risks.signal: Gas turbine and transformer lead times, interconnection queue rulings, data center moratoria in key states, active MW reported by neoclouds.

risks.risk: Memory squeeze and Rubin slip (HBM4 yields, DRAM shortage, higher costs compress margins)
risks.signal: NVIDIA gross margin guide (74% for Q3 FY27, down from 75%); TrendForce HBM and DRAM contract prices; HBM4/HBM4E qualification news.

risks.risk: Supply chain overbuilding and double ordering
risks.signal: Inventory build at NVIDIA ($31.6B) and ODMs, book-to-bill ratios falling, spot memory prices falling below contract.

risks.risk: The biggest AI buyer earns less than the market assumed (OpenAI run rate about $50B vs about $68B reported earlier)
risks.signal: OpenAI run rate and enterprise growth updates; Oracle RPO and OCI capex; CoreWeave backlog and share sales under its 35M share ATM.

indicators.name: Hyperscaler capex guidance (MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META, ORCL)
indicators.why: The source of all downstream demand; 2026 is ~$725B+ and 2027 modeled above $1T.

indicators.name: TSMC monthly revenue
indicators.why: Fastest hard read on AI chip output; Sep 2026 was NT$511.86B, up 54.6% y/y and down 0.6% m/m (reported Oct 8, 2026). Aug 2026 was NT$514.8B, up 53.3% y/y.

indicators.name: Taiwan ODM and supplier monthly sales (Foxconn, Quanta, Wistron, Wiwynn, Delta, AVC)
indicators.why: Shows rack shipments and the Rubin ramp in near real time.

indicators.name: HBM and DRAM contract and spot prices (TrendForce, DRAMeXchange)
indicators.why: Memory is the binding constraint; rising prices help MU and SK hynix and pressure NVIDIA margins.

indicators.name: NVIDIA quarterly results and gross margin guide
indicators.why: Data Center revenue, Rubin mix, inventory and purchase commitments signal supplier orders.

indicators.name: CoWoS capacity and allocation reports
indicators.why: Sets the ceiling for GPU and ASIC unit output and shows NVIDIA vs Broadcom share.
indicators.cadence: Ad hoc, roughly monthly industry reports

indicators.name: Korea export data (semiconductors)
indicators.why: Early proxy for SK hynix and Samsung HBM shipments.
indicators.cadence: Monthly (1st of month, plus 10 and 20 day prints)

indicators.name: ASML and equipment orders, Advantest/Teradyne bookings
indicators.why: Shows whether 2027-2028 capacity is being funded.

indicators.name: Gas turbine backlog and transformer lead times (GEV, Siemens Energy)
indicators.why: Tells how fast new data center power can come online.

indicators.name: Neocloud backlog and financing (CoreWeave, Nebius, Oracle RPO)
indicators.why: Debt-funded demand is the most cyclical part of the buyer base.
